docs.article:
Embed the viewer#

The whole engine drops into any web page with one script tag. It runs in an iframe served from the Verse origin — which carries the cross-origin-isolation headers the engine needs — so your page needs no header changes, works inside any CMS block, and degrades on its own: WebGPU (tiers A/B) → WebGL2 (tier C) → poster image + link-out. The WebGL2 build streams the same scenes, and with the same studio lighting, shadows, bloom and reflection probes; screen-space and ray-traced reflections, path-traced stills and Gaussian splats stay WebGPU-only (Browser support).

You need: a scene id (the ingest/<id>.vpk part of a share link) and a page you can put a <script> tag on. HOST is your Verse origin.

1. The one-line embed#

Code
<script src="https://HOST/embed.js" data-scene="docs-demo-718035483f84"></script>

The viewer mounts into the script's parent element as a div.verse-embed at 16:9, filling the parent's width. Useful attributes:

AttributeEffect
data-poster="poster.jpg"shown until the engine arrives — and if it never does (ad-blocker, offline), the poster stays
data-target="#viewer"mount into that element instead of the script's parent
data-vpk="…" / data-model="…"a .vpk by URL, or a small GLB / splat loaded whole
data-render="continuous"opt out of on-demand rendering (embeds park when nothing changes, so a still viewer costs ~zero battery)
data-hdr="auto"opt in to HDR output on HDR displays; embeds default to SDR so your page's colours never shift uninvited
data-review="1"enable client review pins (see below)
data-share="…"share token for a private scene

2. Programmatic mount: events and control#

Code
<div id="viewer"></div>
<script src="https://HOST/embed.js"></script>
<script>
  const viewer = Verse.embed(document.getElementById("viewer"), {
    scene: "docs-demo-718035483f84",
    poster: "poster.jpg",
  });
  viewer
    .on("ready",    (d) => console.log("tier", d.tier, "first frame in", d.ttfi, "ms"))
    .on("loaded",   (d) => console.log(d.clusters, "clusters, streaming:", d.streamed))
    .on("signed",   (s) => console.log("signature", s.signed))   // true | false | "unverified"
    .on("progress", (p) => console.log("drawn", p.drawn, "of", p.total))
    .on("dwell",    (d) => analytics.track("3d-dwell", { ms: d.ms }))
    .on("error",    (e) => console.warn("verse:", e.message));
</script>

Events already emitted are replayed to late listeners, so attaching after ready fired still delivers it. The full verb and event list — walk(), move(), pick(), setSun(), setMaterial(), play(), goTo(), joinRoom() and the rest — is the Embed SDK reference; the typed contract ships as verse-embed.d.ts next to embed.js.

3. A flythrough video button#

The viewer can record its tour (the compile-time staged tour, or an orbit when the scene has none) to MP4/WebM inside the iframe and hand the bytes to your page. Nothing is uploaded:

Code
progress.hidden = false;
viewer.on("export-progress", (p) => (bar.style.width = `${p.percent}%`));
const r = await viewer.exportVideo({ duration: 10, fps: 30, height: 1080 });
if (!r.cancelled) {
  const a = Object.assign(document.createElement("a"), {
    href: URL.createObjectURL(r.blob),
    download: r.name,                       // "docs-demo-718035483f84-tour.mp4"
  });
  a.click();
}
cancelButton.onclick = () => viewer.cancelExport();   // resolves the promise with { cancelled: true }

Options and the message protocol for non-SDK integrations are in Export a flythrough video.

4. Review pins in the embed#

Opt in with review: true; there is deliberately no built-in button — your page decides how review mode is toggled, the same way it does for walk mode:

Code
const viewer = Verse.embed(el, { scene: "docs-demo-718035483f84", review: true });
reviewToggle.onclick = () => viewer.setReviewMode(reviewToggle.checked);
viewer.on("review-posted",   (d) => console.log("new pin", d.id, d.pos, d.text));
viewer.on("review-selected", (d) => showSidebar(d));
const comments = await viewer.getComments();   // [{ id, t, pos, text, author?, resolved }]

Viewers comment anonymously (an optional name field). Owner moderation — resolve and delete — stays in the playground and /studio; embeds never show those controls. Details: Collect client review comments.

Private scenes#

A private scene needs its share token both for the bytes and for review calls. Pass it once:

Code
const viewer = Verse.embed(el, {
  vpk: "ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk",
  share: "<32 hex shareToken>",
  review: true,
});

Minting tokens: Share privately with tokens.

Styling and layout#

Style div.verse-embed with CSS; it is a normal block element (the live examples on this site set it to position: absolute; inset: 0 inside a 16:9 box). Remove the element to tear the viewer down. The review composer clamps to the iframe's bounds and scrolls internally, so embeds work down to 320 px wide.

Try it#

The Live examples page mounts four real embeds with the exact snippet beside each one; /embed-demo.html is a standalone host page you can view-source.
